metaTitle: Stucco Repair in Southwest Calgary | Sandstone Stucco Co
metaDescription: Stucco repair in Southwest Calgary: cracks, hail, flicker holes and parging. Ask for a no-obligation quote from an independent contractor: (403) 555-0148.
heroSub: From Signal Hill and Shawnessy to Valley Ridge and Bridlewood, stucco homes built from the 1980s on. Tell us what you see on your wall and an independent Calgary stucco contractor will quote it.
introHtml:
Stucco repair in Southwest Calgary starts with working out what kind of wall you have. For this page, southwest means the City's West and South sectors. The City's own neighbourhood labels run from 1980s and 1990s areas such as Signal Hill, Patterson, Millrise and Shawnessy to 2000s ones such as Valley Ridge and Bridlewood, so a repair that suits one wall can be wrong for the next.

Sandstone Stucco Co is an advertising service paid by independent Calgary stucco contractors. It does no stucco work itself and holds no licence, insurance or warranty. The contractor who visits your house quotes and contracts with you directly. Call (403) 555-0148 or send the form for a no-obligation quote.

services.title: Crack and patch repair
services.desc: Hairline cracks, chips and small patches on cement or acrylic finishes. One Calgary contractor, Calgary Parging, lists small patch repairs at $550 to $1,125 before GST; the contractor who sees your wall sets the real figure.

services.title: Hail damage repair estimates
services.desc: A written repair estimate from a contractor that you can pass to your insurer. Your policy and your insurer decide what is covered, and this site does not handle claims.

services.title: Woodpecker hole repair
services.desc: Northern flicker holes patched and reinforced once nesting has ended. Calgary Parging says a typical single patch with reinforcement runs $600 to $800 (GST not stated).

services.title: Parging and window perimeters
services.desc: Cosmetic recoats of the parging at the base of a wall and repairs around windows and doors. Foundation crack repair, waterproofing and structural work are not offered through this page.

sections.heading: Older bungalows, cement stucco and newer infills
sections.html:
Calgary Parging said in 2024 that cement stucco with an acrylic finish is its main product on over 87% of the residential properties it works on, though that is its own job mix and not a city count. A traditional three-coat system, as specified by Imasco, has a scratch coat of at least 10 mm (3/8 inch) and a brown coat that brings the combined system to 19 mm.

Some walls carry a different system, such as EIFS, and the repair method changes with it. Calgary Parging reports that woodpeckers go after EIFS because the foam behind the finish is softer than concrete and sounds hollow when tapped. The contractor who visits can tell you which system your wall is. Our page on stucco repair in Calgary explains how a visit and quote work.

Age matters too. Across the city, 26% of occupied dwellings date from 1961 to 1980 and 12% from 1981 to 1990 (2021 figures), so older homes are common well beyond the southwest. In Signal Hill, a West-sector community, 62% of dwellings were built 1991 to 2000. Imasco notes that some cracking and efflorescence are inherent to portland cement, so not every crack means a failed wall.

sections.heading: Chinooks, freeze-thaw and snow against the wall
sections.html:
The weather figures here are city-wide, but they are what southwest walls go through too. In 2022 Calgary recorded 117 freeze-thaw cycles (the 30-year average is 128) and 54 chinook days (average 46). The City of Calgary says stucco does not handle moisture well, and that moisture and snow can cause it to shrink and crack.

Martini Stone Masonry, a Calgary contractor, reports that snow piled against stucco softens and crumbles the lowest 12 to 18 inches of the wall, and that temperature movement opens gaps of 3 to 8 mm where stucco meets frames. Calgary Parging says over 30% of its residential repairs address water damage from incorrectly installed rain gutters, eaves or flashing. Where your downspouts discharge and where snow piles up are worth a look before the visit.

Timing matters as well. Imasco's guidance is no stucco work when air and substrate temperatures are below 4°C for 24 hours before, during and after application, and Calgary Parging says off-season repairs need heated hoarding. Winter is a sensible time to document damage and collect quotes; ask each contractor what they can do in cold weather and how. See stucco repair cost in Calgary for published price examples.

sections.heading: Hail, woodpeckers and insurance in the southwest
sections.html:
The City of Calgary says all communities in the city are equally exposed to hail, so no corner of the southwest is safe or riskier by default. It also says stucco holds up well to flying debris in moderate wind and hail, but severe storms can cause damage. If you think hail has marked your walls, photograph the damage and call your insurer first. The City advises contacting your home insurance provider before any repair work. A contractor can then give you a written repair estimate to pass along. More detail is on our hail and woodpecker damage page.

Northern flickers are protected under the federal Migratory Birds Convention Act. Calgary Parging says flickers work Calgary stucco hard, especially on west and south elevations in spring. An empty hole with no live bird or viable egg may be repaired without a permit; if a bird is using it, wait until nesting ends. Environment and Climate Change Canada says access can be cut off with a tarp or wire mesh.

Before you sign anything, get written quotes from more than one business and confirm the contractor's City of Calgary business licence by calling 311. A contractor who takes money before finishing the work and solicits the contract in person away from its own premises needs an Alberta prepaid contracting licence, which you can check with Service Alberta. This page is advertising paid by contractors; the site does not file, manage or negotiate insurance claims.

faq.q: What does stucco repair cost in Southwest Calgary?
faq.a: No price is published for Southwest Calgary specifically. As examples, Calgary Parging lists small patch repairs at $550 to $1,125 and medium repairs of two or three areas at $1,250 to $2,650, both before GST. Other Calgary firms publish different figures on their own pages. The contractor who sees your wall sets the actual quote.

faq.q: Is the stucco on my Southwest Calgary bungalow the same as on a newer infill?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Calgary Parging says cement stucco with an acrylic finish covers over 87% of the homes it works on, but some walls are EIFS, which is repaired differently. Ask the contractor to identify the system before quoting, and make sure the materials and work are written into the contract.

faq.q: Can stucco be repaired in winter in Southwest Calgary?
faq.a: Guidance from suppliers is cautious. Imasco says no stucco work below 4°C in air and substrate for 24 hours before, during and after application, and Calgary Parging says stucco cures best above 5°C in dry conditions, typically April through October. Winter is a good time to have damage assessed and quoted. Ask any contractor who offers cold-weather work how they protect the wall.

faq.q: I have hail damage on my Southwest Calgary home. Can Sandstone Stucco Co help with the claim?
faq.a: No. This site is advertising and does not file, manage or negotiate insurance claims. Call your insurer first, take photos and keep your receipts, as the Insurance Bureau of Canada advises. A contractor can give you a written repair estimate you may pass to your insurer, and whether hail damage is covered depends on your own policy.
